content.user_title: Classify Cold Email Replies and Prioritize Follow-Up
content.value_statement: Cold email reply queues mix buying interest, uncertainty, rejection, and automated responses. This skill provides classification rules and routing guidance, with deterministic execution requiring a separate classifier script.
actual_capabilities: Defines buy-signal, positive, neutral, and not-interested categories with example intent phrases.
Documents timing, reply length, question count, and calendar or asset requests as classification features.
Identifies out-of-office indicators for a separate auto-reply category excluded from routing.
Provides a scoring report format covering category, confidence, evidence, and configured routing recommendations.
Documents batch processing through a separately referenced Python classifier.
Specifies human review for confidence below 0.6, including ambiguous, non-English, and context-dependent replies.
limitations: The audited package contains only SKILL.md; the classifier, lexicon, related workflow, and brand configuration are not included.
Documented accuracy and speed claims cannot be verified from the supplied package.
The described lexicon is English-only and may misclassify sarcasm, short replies, or context-dependent language.
Routing examples do not supply Slack or CRM integrations, and deterministic batch processing requires the referenced script, Python, and jq.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Sales Replies
use_cases.description: Identify explicit meeting and pricing requests, then recommend follow-up using the supplied brand routing rules.

use_cases.title: Review a Reply Queue
use_cases.description: Apply the documented batch workflow when dependencies are available, separating automated replies and uncertain classifications.

use_cases.title: Check Campaign Responses
use_cases.description: Distinguish interest, delayed decisions, and rejection while retaining evidence for human review.

prompt_templates.title: Classify One Reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this reply using the documented categories: [reply]. Explain the matched signals. Do not invent a numeric score without the classifier.

prompt_templates.title: Add Timing and Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [reply], received [minutes] after sending, using [routing rules]. Explain the recommended category and route. Report any unavailable dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: combine reply evidence with brand routing.

prompt_templates.title: Review Ambiguous Replies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [replies] for ambiguity, automated responses, and unsubscribe requests. Explain category candidates and flag uncertain cases for human review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect replies that need judgment.

prompt_templates.title: Process a Verified Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: With the reviewed classifier and dependencies available, score [local batch file] using [routing rules]. Summarize results and flag confidence below 0.6.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: run the documented batch workflow with verified dependencies.

output_examples.input: Reply: Please send a calendar link. What is the price? Received 27 minutes after sending. No routing configuration supplied.
output: Evidence: explicit calendar and pricing requests.
Numeric confidence: unavailable without the classifier.
Recommended routing: request the brand routing configuration before selecting a destination.

output_examples.input: Reply: I am out of office until Monday. Received two minutes after sending.
output: Evidence: explicit out-of-office language and rapid response timing.
Recommended routing: exclude from normal reply routing.

output_examples.input: Reply: Maybe later. No additional conversation context supplied.
output: Evidence: delayed interest without a commitment.
Review required: the short reply lacks enough context for confident interpretation.
Numeric confidence: unavailable without the classifier.

best_practices: Verify the referenced classifier and supporting files before executing the batch command.
Supply reply timing and brand routing rules, and remove unnecessary personal information from shared examples.
Review uncertain classifications manually and honor explicit unsubscribe requests.
anti_patterns: Presenting illustrative confidence values or accuracy claims as verified classifier results.
Assuming routing recommendations automatically send messages or create CRM records.
Automatically routing ambiguous or non-English replies without human review.

faq.question: What categories does this skill describe?
faq.answer: It describes buy-signal, positive, neutral, and not-interested, plus an auto-reply category excluded from normal routing.

faq.question: Is the deterministic classifier included?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains only SKILL.md and references a separate Python script and lexicon.

faq.question: Does scoring require an LLM or vendor API?
faq.answer: The documented classifier uses regex and features without LLM or vendor APIs. Its implementation is not included for verification.

faq.question: Can it score a batch of replies?
faq.answer: Batch processing is documented for a local reply file. Execution requires the separate classifier, Python, and jq.

faq.question: When should a person review the result?
faq.answer: The documentation recommends review below 0.6 confidence, especially for short, non-English, sarcastic, or context-dependent replies.

faq.question: Does it automatically update Slack or a CRM?
faq.answer: The document provides routing recommendations based on brand configuration. The supplied package does not include integrations that execute those actions.
